utterances.text: After Hadzic appointed him, do you know whether Badza then reported to Hadzic; or did he continue to report to MUP Serbia; or did he report to both?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: The only times I saw Badza was in the room at meetings. He never reported to me on what he did and where he went. I had two main tasks that I had to accomplish before I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'm just going to rephrase my question. I'm not positive you understood it. After Hadzic appointed Badza, was Hadzic then Badza's superior; did Bogdanovic continue to be Badza's superior; or were both Hadzic and Bogdanovic Badza's superior? Or was there some other situation?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I saw things and as far as I understood things, Goran was above Badza. That's the way I perceived things.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Was your understanding that Badza also continued to be subordinated to Bogdanovic at the time?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of any contacts between him and Bogdanovic. I don't know to this very day whether they took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 52, you said that your task was to record the locations and strength of all forces in the SBWS. I assume that you're referring to Serb forces rather than Croat forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever information I had, I put it on the map. In military terms, I used blue and red colours. I marked check-points, barricades. Whatever I was able to locate, I recorded that on the map. From both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What was the approximate strength of the SBWS TO at that time? Numerical strength.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: In numerical terms, 2- to 3.000. But only 300 to 400 were actually carrying arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What other forces were present on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: The military, the TO, and perhaps some locals who were nowhere. They were civilian protection or something of the sort. That's how I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what was the approximate strength of the military that you've just referred to, at that time?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: The military was in Vukovar and in the barracks. And I believe that their strength was of a battalion. I could be more precise if I were given the map that I drafted and that stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what's the approximate numerical strength of a battalion?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Six hundred to 700.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: How did the geographical area under the control of Serb forces change during your time in the SBWS?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat your question. I don't know what you mean when you say "the geographical area."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: On the day you left the SBWS, did Serb forces control more territory or less territory than on the day you arrived?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single settled area was taken while I was there. There was an attempt to take Bogdanovci. Ilija was wounded on that occasion. And after that I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 58, you said that 40 police officers came to Eastern Slavonia and that they had been tasked by the minister of the interior of the Krajina to set up police stations. When you say "the minister of the interior of the Krajina," are you referring to Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Martic and Boro Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You also said that those police officers then co-ordinated with Zavisic in setting up police stations. So tell me if this is accurate: Milan Martic, as the minister of the interior of the SAO Krajina, along with Boro Bogunovic, sent police officers to the SBWS, where they co-ordinated with Miodrag Zavisic, who was paid by MUP Serbia and appointed by Goran Hadzic to the SBWS TO. I know that's complicated, but can you say whether that's correct or not?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Zavisic was tasked on behalf of the staff to set up police stations in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: All right. Can we now please have document P2452 on the screen. And if this evidence is ever made public, this document should remain confidential, this portion should remain confidential. This is a report dated 9 December 1991 from Jovica Stanisic, as the assistant minister of the interior of Serbia, to the minister of defence of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, please take a moment to read this document, and let me know when you've finished reading it and then I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you able to explain why information from the TO and police of Western Slavonia would go through Jovica Stanisic on its way to the minister of defence of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say anything about the organisation of the state security. I wasn't there, and I am not familiar with the workings of the state security. The only thing I could share with you would be my school knowledge. I've never seen this before, and I will probably not see it again. Since this is going to be confidential, I have not bothered to read this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked to read it. A simple question was put to you. I do understand that you have no explanation for why and how the reporting took place as it appears in this letter. And I would invite you not to consider matters which are exclusively for our court system, to consider them when reading matters, yes or no. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can I ask you, in general terms --

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In general, do you agree that the TO would report directly to a Ministry of Defence rather than to a Ministry of the Interior under normal circumstances; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence was duty-bound to report to somebody. Yugoslavia still existed. And certainly we collected information and intelligence everywhere. In all the territories of Yugoslavia, every intelligence I received about Slavonia, Croatia, or anywhere else, I recorded, and that intelligence would be conveyed through the federal MUP to wherever necessary. In many cases, I wrote --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you. I just want us to get through this as quickly as possible. I'm not asking about your experience. This is a general question based on your knowledge and having lived in the former Yugoslavia. In general terms, normally a TO would report to the Ministry of Defence rather than to the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: When you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to come a bit closer to the microphone so that the interprets can better hear you. Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: During your time in the SBWS TO, did you or anyone else in the TO staff send reports to any of the ministries in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not draft any reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did any of the other four officers who went with you - Badza, Zavisic, Trajkovic, and the others - draft and send reports to any ministry in Serbia or Vojvodina?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, since I was chief, obviously I would have had to have seen reports. So I can tell you that no reports were either drafted or dispatched. Badza spoke to Goran Hadzic and conveyed his messages. That is all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I've finished with this document now. You were asked yesterday about training in Eastern Slavonia. And one of the things you mentioned was that there had been some attempts to train the local population prior to your arrival there. At page 50 of the transcript, you said: "The first time something like that was organised it involved a person who had been training in Golubic training the famous ..." and then there is a word missing from the written transcript. I think I heard you say "Knindze." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That person who arrived at the crossing in a camouflage uniform introduced that way to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was, because it was illegible, whether you said Knindzes. That's my recollection as well. Is that what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I did mention that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You had already heard of Golubic and of the Knindze at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not heard of Golubic, but I did hear of Knindze.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what had you heard about the Knindze in August and September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That those were men who had helped the Serbian people around Knin and in the settled areas there, and that owing the -- to them, the Serbian people had survived in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Who did you learn that from or how did you learn that?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from Ilija Kojic and from my relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And why did you describe the Knindze as famous yesterday? Is it for the reason you've just said, that they had saved the Serb -- the Serbian people around Knin?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That's how I know them. Owing to them, the population of Knin, Benkovac, Obrovac, and Plitvice remained living in that area. And I also know that those were units that operated under Milan Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Was it from Ilija Kojic that you learned that the units operated under Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yesterday you were also asked about three training centres that Mr. Simatovic mentioned in his Kula speech. With respect to Lezimir, you said: "Not a single trainee came to our area, nor do I know that there were any training centres there." You're speaking about the time that you were in Eastern Slavonia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the centre, and not at the crossings where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Right, exactly. So in the places you were, between May and, say, early October of 1991, that was the basis of your knowledge, that period and those places; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about those centres. I only know where Lezimir is, its location. Otherwise, I was never there, and I really don't know that anything was set up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But you can't exclude the possibility that it happened without your knowledge; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speculate, nor do I want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And the same would apply to your conclusions with respect to training in Ilok and Pajzos; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Pajzos is concerned, I still don't know anything about that. I'm here to tell the truth, and that's what I'm doing. As far as Ilok is concerned, I also said that only one person who was with me and mentioned something with this regard was Milovac. I stated that yesterday. I really don't know anything else about those centres. If I knew anything, rest assured that I would tell you, because I'm here to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not in any way questioning your honesty. I'm simply attempting to determine what the basis of your knowledge is. I want to be clear about that. And what the limits of your knowledge are. The same with respect to Vukovar. You mentioned one training centre. You said that's the only one you were aware of. But similarly, you can't exclude the possibility that other training occurred at Vukovar either while you were there or at some later time without your knowledge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that when I collected information about the deployment of the JNA, the TO, the reservists of the JNA, and the police. In Vukovar, I marked just one place where Serbs were deployed and where they controlled the area. That's the place where Captain Kostic was, if I'm not mistaken. The counsel gave me his name, and I agreed that that was him. As for the rest, I really don't know anything. I'm not excluding any possibilities. Things could have been done. But I'm not a person who knows everything. I'm just telling you what I know, even if it costs me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this an appropriate time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is. Mr. Farr, could you give us an indication as to the time you'd still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If I could know how much time I've used, that might help me make an estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- seems to --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: -- not because I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have used little time and you would need only little time to conclude, then I wouldn't expect you to take any more time. If you had taken --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the reason I ask is because I know approximately how I'm getting through my outline, and that will help me know, based what the pace is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... two -- two --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: It's not that I'm determined to use every possible moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two hours and 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Two hours and 10 minutes. I think it will be less than another hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- the last session will be 75 minutes. If it would be possible to conclude your cross-examination in that time, then we could, tomorrow, start with the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I will certainly do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to go back to the Kula camp awards ceremony. Were you actually present in the room when Mr. Simatovic made his speech?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: This ceremony took place in several rooms. When Franko Simatovic was delivering his speech, I was there part of the time. I did not attend the whole ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't -- I didn't quite understand your answer. During Mr. Simatovic's speech, were you present in that room?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, I think this is clear from what you said yesterday. But your assumption that he was bragging was based on your knowledge of the Kula camp itself and when that was constructed. It was that, that led you to believe that the unit was only a year old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And I know because I have classmates who were in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What are the names of your classmates who were in that unit?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Kersmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What's the first name?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: His nickname is Krsman, but I'm hard put to remember the first name. If I remember it later, I'll tell you, but right now I'm drawing a blank.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: When did he join that unit?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was established. In 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Where -- had he fought in the wars in Croatia and Bosnia; and, if so, where?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I know is that he, too, was at one of the check-points from which we controlled the border. But he never mentioned that he was involved anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Which check-point was he present at?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Closer to Ilok, closer to Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But, again, that's a border crossing between Slavonia and Vojvodina; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And did he have approximately the same responsibilities as you when he was at that border crossing?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: How long did he serve at that border crossing?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I think less long than I. I think I'm one of the people who did the longest tour in that border belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: How did he come to move from the public security service of Vojvodina, I assume, to the State Security Service of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: A vacancy was announced. I know there were people from Backo, Petrovo Selo, and I know a couple of men who were in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Other than this Kersmanovic, who else do you know who was in that unit?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: There was Branko Curcic and quite a few other people, but I can't remember many of them now. There was a person nicknamed Dzo [phoen] from Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what did they tell you about when this unit was founded?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: We attended this anniversary celebration. That means one year before. That's what I know about the unit and its establishment. It's certain that they had not been established before at Kula; I guarantee that with my life, because those used to be premises for accommodating refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. So you know personally that the unit had not been at Kula before that camp was established. All the rest of your information about the unit comes from these people who you know who were in the unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. So going back to your time in Eastern Slavonia, in paragraph 60 of your statement, you discuss the first attack on Bogdanovci in which Ilija Kojic was wounded and in which Arkan also participated. Am I right that this was a combined operation of the TO and Arkan's Men?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The TO did not participate, apart from Arkan and one tank from the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Why was Ilija Kojic present?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: He obviously came to see how it was going on. He found himself in cross-fire. And after that, there was an attempt to rescue him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did he still have a position with the TO at that point? You said that he had been commander earlier, before Badza.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He still played that role. He and Badza handled all this. And after he was wounded, Badza took over the whole thing. That's how I see it. Although Badza had this order from Goran Hadzic, I believe the two of them led that, this thing, on their own.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, I have some difficulties understanding the answer as it appears on page 60, line 6. If it's clear to you as an answer to your question, then I will further think about it; but if it's as unclear to me as it is to you, then perhaps we should seek clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'll address that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, the answer that Judge Orie was referring to, you were asked: "Am I right that this was a combined operation of the TO and Arkan's Men?" And you said: "No. The TO did not participate, apart from Arkan and one tank from the JNA." Maybe the best way to ask it is: Who participated in the attack on Bogdanovci?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Arkan and one tank that was somehow resubordinated or given them. Those were the people who were involved in that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. So it was Arkan, his men, one tank that was resubordinated to Arkan by the JNA, and Ilija Kojic, who had a position with the TO, was present; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Ilija Kojic was not involved in the operation. He came after a while to see what was going on. If he had been involved, he wouldn't have ended up as he did. He would have known where everyone was. The way it was, he walked into a cross-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, if that's clear now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: At paragraph 62 of your statement, you describe an incident involving Rajo Bozovic. In essence, it sounds to me like the story you recount in that paragraph is one of Bozovic's group attempting to interfere with the administration of justice for personal reasons. Is that a fair summary of that incident?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, which paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps in this instance my learned friend could show him the paragraph, which hasn't been referred to before.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sure. Yeah, that's a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we could have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yeah, it's D34. And the paragraph number is --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's 66, not 62.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Ah, yes. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, if you -- if you feel like you need to take a moment to read the paragraph, do so; otherwise, I can ask my question.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: You can ask your question, because I wrote this, and I'm only telling the truth in this statement as in my evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, you may ask the question. If there's no need, if you say "I'm ready, I've read it," then Mr. Farr will put his question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not interested in the specific details of what happened, but it seems to me that this is essentially a story of Bozovic's group trying to interfere with the administration of justice for personal reasons. Is that a fair summary of this incident, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: They thought they would take the law in their own hands, but I didn't let them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And they tried to take the law into their own hands in a violent and threatening way; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What is your personal impression of Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my first encounter with him, and the result was that I enforced the law according to the current legislation. What kind of impression could I have of a man who takes law into his own hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Right. The answer is obvious, and it's that you had a very bad impression of him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You said that after you'd disarmed Rajo Bozovic and six people you sent them back to Croatia, either to Erdut or some other place. Now, Bozovic is from Montenegro. Why did you send him to Croatia rather than to Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not send him either to Croatia or to Montenegro. I disarmed him and turned the weapons over to Srbobran, because that not my SUP. Colleagues from Novi Sad called me. I did that job and then turned him over to the competent SUP, the one in Srbobran, to the officers who were in charge, who had authority to conduct further investigation. I'm only the one who enabled them to do so, because they had not been able to do it themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it your belief or do you have information that he, after this incident, went to Croatia, either to Erdut or some other place?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the information I was given by the commander of that station, in Srbobran. It was my job to disarm them, arrest them. And I did that and handed them over. He later told me that he had written up a criminal report against all of them, listing all the charges according to the current legislation, and then he released them after consultations with the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And did that commander of the station in Srbobran tell you that Bozovic had gone to Croatia, to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the basis on which I wrote this passage in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did he tell you why Bozovic was going to Erdut?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now at the time this incident happened, what was your understanding of why Rajo Bozovic was in Vojvodina in the first place?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the reason why all of that happened in the first place, that one of his colleagues had a criminal report filed against him for attack against an authorised official.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't quite understand that. Before this incident that you describe in paragraph 66, did Rajo Bozovic come from Croatia to Vojvodina and then the incident happened and then he returned to Croatia? Is that the correct chronology?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: One man out of the six or seven who were with Rajo Bozovic had been in Srbobran six or seven days prior. That man was a native of Srbobran. And when he came there, he found that his mother had a relationship with a certain man. He beat up that man. The police wrote up a criminal report against that young man. The young man complained to Rajo Bozovic. And after that, they came and did what they did. And after that, I did my job as I was required, professionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. So if you know, how had Rajo Bozovic come to be in Vojvodina at that time in the first place? In other words, why was he there on the day of that incident?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: He had come intending to create an incident, to have a settlement of accounts with an operative policeman who had only done his job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bozovic is around with a group. Now, that group was, at least that is what Mr. Farr thinks, was not formed to deal with all these matters. Why was Mr. Bozovic in the area at all with a group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He had not been in Srbobran in the days before. He just arrived in Srbobran that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where had he been the days before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why was he with a group arriving in Srbobran?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To settle accounts with an operative who had filed a criminal complaint against a member of his group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That was a criminal complaint on the basis of the incident where one of the members of the group had attacked the man who had a relationship with his mother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That had happened how much time before he came to settle the account?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two or three days before. Perhaps a day before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, why was Mr. Bozovic in the area with a group of men at the moment when one of the members of that group attacked a man who he thought had a relationship with his mother? Why was he there three days before? Why was Mr. Bozovic around with the group? Because you don't need a group nor a leader to -- to attack someone who has a relationship with your mother. Why was he there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's obviously a misunderstanding. The incident created by one individual from his group was a native of Srbobran. He was staying with his mother in his own house. The mother had personal reasons to see that man. Her son, who was in Rajo's group, objected to that and beat up that man. The man complained to the police. The police did their job and took into custody the son.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the existence of the group? That man was a member of, as you said, Rajo's group. What was that group doing? What was the activity of that group? I think, Mr. Farr, that that's what you'd like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the first time I had any contact with that group. I really don't know where he had come from or who he was. I was just told that there was an armed group who had barged into the police station and attacked an operative policeman. I took my men to Srbobran and did my job, as I described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I understand you well, you only have knowledge about what followed on from the attack on this man having a relationship with one of the group member's mother and that you have no knowledge whatsoever about the armed group led by Mr. Bozovic, their activities, whereabouts. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know that. I was given a specific task which I carried out, and I recorded everything, including the criminal report that I filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered the question. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware that Rajo Bozovic was at the Kula awards ceremony in 1997?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you see him shake hands with Slobodan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Then I take it you didn't hear Milosevic tell Bozovic that he had read Bozovic's reports.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in a video-clip. I wasn't there, so obviously I couldn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony, did you just read the transcripts of the video or did you actually look at the video itself?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Both. I read the transcripts and I watched the clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd now like to play a portion of P61 which is the video of the Kula reach. This is going to be the portion from 13 minutes and 4 seconds to 13 minutes and 42 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And we won't start just yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcripts have been provided to the booth?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We'll doing it without sound, Your Honour. It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without -- just -- so they're without sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, at the same time, does that mean that the witness doesn't hear anything, or should he take his earphones off?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: He should take his earphones off, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please take your earphones off and only look at the screen, what you see there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I apologise, but there is one instruction I'd like to give him before he takes his earphones off, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please to so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm going to ask you to do is watch this video. The video shows people listening to Frenki's speech. And I want you to try to see whether you see yourself in this video. If you do, please note the time code which will be at the bottom of the screen, and then when the clip finishes playing, you can tell us whether you saw yourself and, if so, at which time code. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So then, Mr. Laugel, could you please begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, did you see yourself in that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I wasn't present when Franko was speaking there. There were several places where decorations were awarded. I was not in this particular place that you showed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification. All right. At paragraph 60 of your statement, you say that Arkan and Goran Hadzic had a close and friendly relationship. Can you describe this relationship in more detail, if you're able to?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was billeted in Erdut, Goran Hadzic, every time when he came to the centre, he would go to the upper floor where Arkan was and he spent time with him. He would not spend a lot of time with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So how often would Goran Hadzic and Arkan see each other during the time you were at the Erdut centre?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I could say two to three times a week. But let's say it was two times a week, on average. I'm talking about the centre itself. I don't know if they met anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: All right. That was going to be my next question. You also said that Arkan provided security for Hadzic. Can you tell us about this? Was Arkan personally involved in Hadzic's security? Did he assign his men to secure Hadzic? Did both of those things happen? What was that arrangement?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: He had men as part of Goran's security detail. People who served as Goran's body-guard were supplied with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did Arkan ever personally serve as Hadzic's body-guard, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he didn't. Knowing Arkan and his mentality, it would have been a sheer humiliation for Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And why do you say -- did you say that it would be a humiliation for Arkan?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a very high opinion of himself. At least that's how I saw Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So being a body-guard would be too lowly a position for him.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the fact that Arkan provided Hadzic's security people shows that there was a significant amount of trust between Hadzic and Arkan?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Trust or fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I would now like to look at document 1D1630. This is a document from the Stanisic Defence exhibit list. I'm not sure whether it needs to be kept under seal if this evidence becomes public later. This was one of the documents on the chart, so it's one that would be included in that range of reserved MFI numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment, please, while I find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a look at it and then we'll put on the record, and let's not forget about it, whether it needs, under all circumstances, to be under seal or whether it could ever become public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So in the meantime, if we could have it on e-court, please. And just for the Chamber's reference, this document purports to be an order signed by Goran Hadzic appointing Arkan as the commander of the TO training centre at Erdut, not of the TO itself but of the training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I know that the Defence showed you this document during your proofing and you said that you didn't know that Hadzic had appointed Arkan to this position. I'd like to draw your attention to the signature at the bottom of this document. Are you able to recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Goran Hadzic's signature. I came across Goran's signature quite often, and I can claim with 90 per cent certainty that this is also his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And if we could zoom out and look at the document as a whole again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Does this document appear to be authentic to you?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It looks authentic. It was drafted at the time when we were about to leave the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Am I correct that the number 1/91 at the upper left-hand corner of the document means that this is the first decision rendered by Goran Hadzic after officially becoming president of the government of the AO of SBWS?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, given the number 1. It would be only logical to assume that that was the first document he ever issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know why appointing Arkan to this position would be so important as to be Hadzic's first decision in this position?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, in order to protect himself. And when I say "himself," I mean Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know what the best approach with this document is. It's within the range of MFI documents that's on the chart. I suppose I can say the Prosecution doesn't oppose admission of it if it's tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, could you tell us already which pre-assigned number this document has received on your list or will receive on your list?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document has pre-assigned number D339, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's on the record that D339, a pre-assigned number, meets no objection for admission by the Prosecution. Please proceed. Or perhaps we -- it's easier to just admit it into evidence, unless the Simatovic Defence would have any ... no. Mr. Jordash, therefore, D339 as pre-assigned --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is admitted into evidence. Mr. Farr, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, in reviewing another document that the Defence showed you, you said, quote --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And for the Chamber's reference, this is page 2 of the chart regarding Exhibit P329.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You said: "I do not know that Arkan was taking some people away and killing them. I assume it's true since there are a lot of people who mention that." I think that's a relatively clear statement, but I just want to confirm that you don't have any reason to doubt that Arkan killed people while he was present in Eastern Slavonia, including prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard stories while I was in Erdut. If I had known it at the time, rest assured, I would have taken it up with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: When did you hear those stories?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Subsequently at various celebrations. It was hearsay. At the moment when I was there in the area, I didn't know. Because if I had known, I would have done what was best for the Serbian people. Rest assured of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What did you hear about Arkan killing prisoners at these various celebrations after you left Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you. There were stories about him being very brutal in combat, about taking prisoners. Those were all stories, rumours. Nobody ever mentioned any names. But as those stories circulated, some of them reached me as well. I can't be any more specific. I knew a lot of people because I had spent nearly six months in the area. I still had contact with a lot of people from the area. And the stories still circulate and are being listened to and recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. In paragraph 62 of your statement, you say that you know, from what Badza told you after meetings, that the TO staff had contact with Goran Hadzic. Am I correct that this means that Badza met with Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The two of them did meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: How often did they meet?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that with any degree of certainty. In any case, there were briefings every evening when we reported of what we had done and what our -- our plan was for the following day. But Badza often reported about meeting with Hadzic, and we talked about the setting up of police stations and the rest of the three or four basic tasks that we had been given before we crossed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. You said Badza often talked about -- often reported about meeting with Hadzic. In those reports, did he tell you what they had discussed, what Badza and Hadzic had discussed?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Badza is not a man of many words. He mostly told us what to do. As to what he did and with whom, he would only tell us, I had a discussion with Goran and we have to do this and that, based on which I concluded that Goran was above Badza or that Goran backed up Badza, in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we now please have document 1D253. And, once again, I don't know whether this would need to be kept confidential if this evidence becomes public. This document purports to be an award from Major-General Andrija Biorcevic of the JNA 12th Corps to Radovan Stojcic, Badza; Zivko Trajkovic; and Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan. It's dated 23rd November 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, would you include this document in your list on which we expect you to say whether it should be kept confidential?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Neither this or the document we looked at before should be or need to be confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If -- therefore, it should not be exempted if the testimony would ever become public. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, could you please take a moment to read this brief document and focus in particular on the positions listed for the three men, and just let me know when you've finished reading.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The post that is listed for Badza in this document, that's consistent with your knowledge of the position that Badza actually held at the time you were in Eastern Slavonia; correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the post, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And the same is true for Zivko Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, this document seems to indicate that the TO of the SBWS and Arkan fought together with the 12th Corps of the JNA in the fight to liberate Borovo. Did you ever hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I was no longer there at the time. I have not seen this before. I don't know what to say. I've told you what I know. I've never seen Zeljko's post spelled out before, so I really don't know what to tell you. If you think that there may be something I know, ask me. I'll be very sincere and honest and I'll tell you what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sure. This kind of goes back to what you had said a few moments ago about how you still, even today, have a lot of contacts in this region. I realize this is after you left, but did you ever hear anything about the combat to liberate Borovo that's consistent with this document, which indicates that the 12th Corps of the JNA fought along with the SBWS TO and Arkan? Have you ever heard anything about that?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: When I returned from Erdut, I was quite involved with my family. I had other commitments, so I was really not very much interested in all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not asking what else you did. We ask you whether you have any knowledge of combined operational action between the JNA, the TO, and Arkan. Do you have any knowledge about that? Tell us. If not, you have no knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We never conducted any such actions while I was there. I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we zoom in on the signature of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any way of recognising the signature or the stamp on this document?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I never received any documents from this gentleman Biorcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know whether Andrija Biorcevic was, in fact, the commander of the JNA 12th Corps during your time in Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender this as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. This is not on the -- I think we asked the Stanisic Defence whether there was any reason to ... was it on your list? Was any number pre-assigned? It was not. Then it receives a Prosecution exhibit number. Madam Registrar, that would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit P3010, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against admission? If not, P3010 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 61 of your statement, you indicated that the members of the TO staff worked and slept in the same building where Arkan was located but in a different section. I think a moment ago you said something about the second floor. Can you describe where the TO was in that building and where Arkan and his men were in that building.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: We had one part of the lower floor. That's where our rooms were. And there was also an office, a corner room served as an office. Well, Arkan was a bit further away -- actually, his men were a bit further away, and Arkan himself was on the upper floor above us.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So Arkan was in the same building as you. Were his men also in the same building as you?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Only a few. The others occupied some other premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But Arkan's Men provided security for the entire building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this indicates that there was at least some degree of trust between Arkan and Badza, the fact that Badza was happy to have this building secured by Arkan's Men?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that Badza maybe trusted him; and as for the rest of us, we didn't. And that's why we wanted to be relocated. Badza always claimed that he could handle the situation and that that was his responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So while there was tension between part of the TO staff and Arkan, Badza and Arkan, at least, got on better than the rest of you did with Arkan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 65 of your statement, and just now, you've indicated that all of you complained to Badza that you weren't happy being in the same place as Arkan. Why did you think Badza would be able to do something about that situation?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander. He was the one who had to deal with the problem. We informed him that there was a problem, and he was the one who was supposed to tell us what to do, and we would have done it. However, we insisted that we did not want to be there. I knew very little about Arkan, but the group of 16 policemen knew a lot more, and that's why we insisted, because they knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it true that Badza was best placed to deal with Arkan not just as a commander but also because he had a better relationship with Arkan than the rest of you did?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Very few of us, and only rarely, had anything to do with him. And when I say "him," I mean Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please have D31 on the screen now. Page 1 in both languages. And could I also ask that this comment chart, which is the witness's comment chart that's been admitted as D336, be handed to the witness so he's able to look at the document and at his comment about it at the same time. And we're interested specifically in the bottom paragraph in the English, which is the second paragraph in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat which number is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: This is the first document on the chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And since you've looked at this document before, I'll just quote from it. It says that Arkan stated that: "Weaponry, ammunition, and MES," which stands for mines and explosives, "had been supplied by the MUP and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia and that he had been distributing them to the TO staffs in Erdut, Sarvas, and Borovo Selo ..." Your comment was that: "This was impossible because the MUP did not have the mentioned supplies in its warehouse." You went on to say that the MUP had only "pistols, automatic/semi-automatic rifles, and rifles." Now I take it you'll agree with me that pistols, automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles are all weapons; correct? My point is that you intended to refer only to the last item, the mines and explosives, when you said that the MUP did not have those items.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did not have mines and explosives in our police force. The police only had automatic/semi-automatic rifles and pistols. That's the weapons our police still has. I know, as a member of the staff, that in order to equip and train this one unit, we had asked Badza to let us have this equipment but we were not able to get equipment, weapons, or uniforms. Anything. While I was there, not a single rifle, not a single uniform, was delivered to that staff. I mean the staff where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Zeljko Raznjatovic I exclude from this, because I was in conflict with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted to clarify that your comment, where you say "this cannot be true because the MUP didn't have the mentioned supplies," you were referring only to mines and explosives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. But I suppose that Badza would have found it easier to get this than Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now have, please, P334 on the screen, page 1 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, sir, for your reference, this is the second document that you commented on in your chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And here we're interested in numbered paragraph 1 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, this document describes several incidents in which Arkan killed prisoners. As I read it, it describes four incidents. In the first two, they were both taken from the Dalj Police Station. And one group of those was killed at the Danube; one group was killed at the Dalj Police Station. And then it describes two other killing incidents in which the location is not specified. Your comment on this document was: "This also relates to the fact that Arkan was in Erdut and to the allegation that he was taking away and killing detainees. That could not happen while I was in the centre because there were too many people at the centre and there were no shootings at the centre." Sir, I just want to confirm that your evidence is that all you can say with certainty is that Arkan didn't kill people at the Erdut centre during the period you were there.

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: The centre of Erdut is a very small area. Every time, I would sound the alert and we would go out. If I had known that Arkan was doing this, I would have reacted. At the centre I was, nobody did anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't the question. You said it could not have happened because I would have known. Now, paragraph 1, at least, describes what happened in Dalj, where people were detained and killed. Your comment focuses on what could have happened, according to your knowledge, in the Erdut centre. Whereas what is described here did not happen in the Erdut centre. That is what Mr. Farr is interested to know, that your comment is not relevant for the events described, because your explanation and your comment is about what you should have been aware of if it would have happened in the camp, but what is described did not happen in the camp; and, therefore, the two do not match. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... okay --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not aware of that information about Zeljko doing something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we now have P1078 on the screen, the top half of page 2 in B/C/S and the bottom of page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not really legible. It's very hard to make out. But I think I've read this document before. In fact, I read it a couple of days ago. And it relates to what Zeljko Raznjatovic brought to the centre or had received from someone. I can't make out this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not sure we're on the right page, and maybe -- maybe we don't even need to look at the document. I can just quote it to you. The document catalogues some of the weapons that Arkan and his men had. It says: "In addition to automatic rifles the, the detachment has two tanks, two triple-barrelled 20-millimetre anti-aircraft guns, Zoljas, and sniper rifles with night sights and silencers." Your comment on this was - and, again, this is it page 1 of the chart: "It is true, aside from the allegation that the MUP was providing weapons, because we did not have lorries or the mentioned weapons." The only point I want to make is that your comment should be limited to weapons other than automatic rifles because, as you've just confirmed, the MUP did have automatic rifles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that he guarded the MUP. That's certainly not my evidence. The MUP did not have lorries or cannons or jeeps or planes. It might be a mistake here. But if it is, I correct it now, and I'm saying, none of this correct [as interpreted]. The MUP did not provide whatsoever to Zeljko. If it had been up to me, I wouldn't have given him bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I apologise, it should actually be the bottom of page 2 in English. That's my fault.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, the point was different. It -- it concerns just your comment on this document. And your comment was the MUP does not have the kind of weapons listed. One of the kinds of weapons listed is automatic rifles, which you have said that the MUP does have. My question is: Is your comment, therefore, limited? What you intended to say was that the MUP could not have supplied tanks, anti-aircraft guns, Zoljas, and sniper rifles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give only what I have. I can't give what I don't have. The MUP did not have that among its assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Right. Whereas the MUP did have automatic rifle among its assets; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DST-074[Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I emphasised several times and enumerated what kind of weapons we have, today.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, thank you very much for your patience with my questions today.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've finished. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farr. I suggest to the parties that we continue tomorrow. Witness DST-074, we'll continue tomorrow, when you'll be re-examined and perhaps further cross-examined. Mr. Jordash, could you give us any indication as how much time you would need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thirty minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thirty minutes. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the time being I have only one question or, rather, one topic I want to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I expect that we could conclude the evidence of this evidence, because I still have to consult with my colleagues, somewhere during the first session. Yes. Witness DST-074, we'll continue tomorrow, 9.00, in this same Courtroom II. I again instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in any other way with anyone about your testimony, whether that's testimony given yesterday and today or testimony still to be given tomorrow. And we expect that it will not take much more than one hour tomorrow morning. Could you please follow the usher before we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll adjourn for the day. And we'll resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 18th of August, 9.00 in the morning in this same Courtroom II. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of August, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Closed session]  [Confidentiality partially lifted by order of the Chamber]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
